tools.duckduckgo_web_search: Performs a web search using the DuckDuckGo API, ideal for general queries, news, articles, and online content. Use this for broad information gathering, recent events, or when you need diverse web sources. Supports content filtering and region-specific searches. Maximum 10 results per request.
tools.web_browse: Retrieves the HTML content of a specified web page. Use this to fetch and analyze web content from a given URL.

tools.analyze_laravel_project:
This tool analyzes a Laravel project to identify changes needed for upgrading to a newer version.
    
    It scans the project structure, identifies files requiring updates, analyzes dependencies, and checks for deprecated features.
tools.analyze_laravel_file:
This tool analyzes a specific file in a Laravel project to identify changes needed for upgrading to a newer version.
    
    It examines the file content and provides specific recommendations for upgrading.
tools.fetch_laravel_upgrade_guide:
This tool fetches the official Laravel upgrade guide for a specific version.
    
    It retrieves the upgrade documentation and extracts key sections like dependency changes, high impact changes, etc.

tools.start-sms-verification: Start new phone number verification requests. If the request is successful, you should ask the user to enter the OTP they received on the phone number we are verifying.
tools.report-sms-verification: Report the received verification code to verify it, using the phone number of the user
tools.number-lookup: With quick and easy access to Number Lookup, you can enhance your communications and keep your database as clean as a whistle. Number Lookup checks against first-party numbering sources and provides real-time feedback. Test numbers to ensure your recipients are ready and waiting to receive your messages!
tools.send-text-message: Send a text message to a contact on the specified channel. The contact can be a phone number in E.164 format, or the identifier for the specified channel.
tools.send-media-message: Send a media message from URL given in parameter to a contact on the specified channel. The contact can be a phone number in E.164 format, or the identifier for the specified channel. The media must be specified with its URL.
tools.send-location-message: Send a location message from an address given in parameter to a contact on the specified channel. The contact can be a phone number in E.164 format, or the identifier for the specified channel.
tools.send-choice-message: Send a choice message to the user. The choice message can contain up to 3 choices if not text or up to 10 message if text only. Each choice can be a call message (phone number + title to display next to it), a location message (latitude / longitude + title to display next to it), a text message or a URL message (the URL to click on + title to display next to it). The contact can be a phone number in E.164 format, or the identifier for the specified channel.
tools.send-template-message: Send a template message to a contact on the specified channel. The contact can be a phone number in E.164 format, or the identifier for the specified channel.
tools.send-whatsapp-template-message: Send a template message to a contact (phone number in E.164 format) on the WhatsApp channel.
tools.list-conversation-apps: Get a list of all Conversation apps in the account. Apps are created and configured in the Sinch Dashboard or with the Conversation API. The App is the entity that holds the credentials related to the various channels
tools.list-messaging-templates: Get a list of all messaging-related templates (omni-channel or channel specific) belonging to an account. Note that the Email templates are NOT included in this list - they can be found with another tool: list-email-templates. Do not try to use this tool to list Email templates, it will not work.
tools.tts-callout: Make a callout with a Text-To-Speech prompt
tools.get-call-information: Get information about a call using its ID
tools.conference-callout: Call a phone number and connects it to a conference room when answered
tools.manage-conference-participant: Manage a conference participant. The conference is identified by the conference Id used in the callout, and the participants by the callId associated to their phone number when the conference callout to their number was made
tools.send-email: Send an email to a recipient with a subject and body.
tools.retrieve-email-info: Retrieve the content of an email and the events that happened thanks to its ID
tools.list-email-templates: Get a list of Email templates from Mailgun for a specific domain. Note that the Messaging templates (omni-channel or channel-specific such as WhatsApp) are NOT included in this list - they can be found with another tool: list-messaging-templates. Do not try to use this tool to list Messaging templates, it will not work.
tools.list-email-events: Get a list of email events from Mailgun for a specific domain. You can filter by event type and limit the number of results.
tools.analytics-metrics: Get email analytics metrics from Mailgun for an account. All parameters are optional. You can filter by domain, metrics type and specify a time range. By default, it will return all metrics for all your domains for the last 7 days.
tools.list-available-regions: Lists all regions for numbers provided for the project ID.
tools.list-rented-numbers: Lists all active numbers for a project.
tools.rent-sinch-virtual-numbers: Activates a phone number that matches the search criteria provided in the request. Currently the rentAny operation works only for US LOCAL numbers
tools.search-for-available-numbers: Search for available phone numbers that are available for you to activate. You can filter by any property on the available number resource.

tools.get_entity_set_ids: Get all available entity set IDs configured in the application
tools.get_supported_model_ids: Get all available supported model IDs for a specific entity set
tools.get_entity_set_details: Get detailed information about a specific entity set including corpus information, labels, and supported models
tools.get_supported_model_details: Get detailed information about a specific supported model
tools.detect_entities: Detect named entities in German text using a specified NER model and entity set
tools.detect_entities_and_pseudonymize: Detect named entities in German text and pseudonymize the detected entities

tools.seats_cached_search:
Search cached award availability between origin/destination pairs.

    Use this tool to quickly explore cached inventory exposed by the Seats.aero Partner API.
    Provide at least one origin and destination airport code. Narrow the response with
    optional dates, mileage sources, cabins, and pagination controls. Results include
    pagination metadata so you can request additional pages by passing the `cursor` or
    adjusting `skip`.
tools.seats_bulk_availability:
Retrieve high-volume availability data for a single mileage program.

    Use this when you need broad scans of a specific loyalty program. The endpoint supports
    pagination via `cursor`/`skip`, as well as filters for cabin, date range, and regions.
    This dataset can be large, so prefer tighter filters when possible.
tools.seats_list_routes: List normalized routes tracked by Seats.aero, optionally filtered by mileage program.
tools.seats_trip_details: Fetch flight-level itinerary details for a cached availability record.

tools.ado_configure: Configura la conexión a Azure DevOps con token de acceso personal (PAT).
tools.ado_get_work_item: Obtiene un Work Item de Azure DevOps por su ID
tools.ado_query_sprint: Consulta User Stories de un sprint específico en Azure DevOps
tools.ado_query_area: Consulta User Stories de un área específica en Azure DevOps
tools.ado_query_wiql: Ejecuta una consulta WIQL personalizada en Azure DevOps
tools.ado_get_work_item_type_fields: Obtiene los campos disponibles y requeridos para un tipo de Work Item
tools.ado_create_work_item: Crea un nuevo Work Item en Azure DevOps. Usa ado_get_work_item_type_fields para ver campos requeridos.
tools.ado_update_work_item: Actualiza un Work Item existente en Azure DevOps
tools.ado_delete_work_item: Elimina un Work Item en Azure DevOps. Por defecto realiza borrado lógico; usa destroy=true solo para eliminación permanente.
tools.ado_add_work_item_link: Crea una relación (Parent/Child/Related/Duplicate/Successor/Predecessor) entre dos Work Items de Azure DevOps.
tools.ado_remove_work_item_link: Elimina una relación existente entre dos Work Items de Azure DevOps.
tools.ado_list_iterations: Lista las iteraciones/sprints disponibles en el proyecto
tools.ado_list_areas: Lista las áreas disponibles en el proyecto
tools.ado_add_comment: Agrega un comentario/entrada de discusión a un Work Item. Soporta formato Markdown y menciones. Para mencionar usuarios, primero usa ado_search_users para obtener el ID de identidad (UUID), luego inclúyelo en el campo mentions. En el texto del comentario, escribe @{displayName} donde quieras la mención.
tools.ado_get_comments: Obtiene los comentarios/historial de discusión de un Work Item. Incluye menciones resueltas.
tools.ado_search_users: Busca usuarios en Azure DevOps por nombre o email. Devuelve el ID de identidad (UUID) necesario para menciones en comentarios (@{name}) y otras operaciones. Usa el resultado en ado_add_comment con el campo mentions.
tools.ado_upload_attachment: Sube un archivo como adjunto a Azure DevOps y devuelve la URL del adjunto
tools.ado_add_attachment: Agrega un adjunto a un Work Item existente. Maneja automáticamente concurrencia cuando múltiples adjuntos se agregan al mismo WI.
tools.ado_delete_attachment: Elimina un adjunto de un Work Item removiendo su relación. Maneja automáticamente concurrencia cuando múltiples cambios afectan el mismo WI.
tools.ado_get_attachments: Obtiene la lista de adjuntos de un Work Item
tools.ado_list_repositories: Lista todos los repositorios Git del proyecto.
tools.ado_get_repository: Obtiene detalles de un repositorio específico por nombre o ID.
tools.ado_list_branches: Lista las ramas (branches) de un repositorio.
tools.ado_list_pull_requests: Lista Pull Requests con filtros opcionales. Busca por repositorio o en todo el proyecto.
tools.ado_get_pull_request: Obtiene detalles completos de un Pull Request.
tools.ado_update_pull_request: Actualiza propiedades de un Pull Request (título, descripción, estado de borrador).
tools.ado_abandon_pull_request: Abandona un Pull Request (cambia estado a Abandoned).
tools.ado_get_pull_request_reviewers: Obtiene todos los revisores y sus votos de un Pull Request.
tools.ado_add_pull_request_reviewer: Agrega un revisor a un Pull Request.
tools.ado_get_pull_request_threads: Obtiene todos los hilos de comentarios de un Pull Request.
tools.ado_create_pull_request_thread: Crea un nuevo hilo de comentarios (comentario general o comentario de código).
tools.ado_reply_to_pull_request_thread: Responde a un hilo de comentarios existente.
tools.ado_get_pull_request_commits: Obtiene todos los commits de un Pull Request.
tools.ado_get_pull_request_work_items: Obtiene los work items vinculados a un Pull Request.
tools.ado_update_pull_request_thread_status: Actualiza el estado de un hilo de comentarios (ej: marcar como Fixed, WontFix, etc.).

tools.upsertEmailAccount: 新增或更新邮件账户，支持IMAP/SMTP配置。默认支持yeah、qq、163、126、新浪、搜狐这6个邮箱服务的IMAP/SMTP配置，其他邮箱服务需要自行去官方获取IMAP/SMTP配置信息。
tools.deleteEmailAccount: 删除邮件账户，支持通过accountId或email删除
tools.getEmailAccounts: 获取邮件账户，支持通过accountId或email获取特定账户，如果都不指定则获取所有账户
tools.fetchAndSaveEmails: 自动拉取并保存新邮件
tools.extractBodyFromText: 提取纯净正文（去除引用内容）
tools.formatEmailContent: 按指定格式整理邮件内容，返回格式化提示词
tools.getFormattedEmails: 获取整理后邮件内容（分页、搜索、联合附件表）
tools.addTemplate: 添加邮件模版（发送/回复）
tools.createNotification: 创建通知（只接收type, content, priority, extra_data参数）
tools.addOrUpdateSignature: 添加或更新签名（只根据accountId或email查找账户并更新config.signature）
tools.getAllRecipients: 获取指定邮件的所有收件人
tools.updateEmailAccountConfig: 更新邮件账户的配置信息（imap/smtp），支持accountId或email
tools.replyEmail: 回复指定邮件，支持自定义正文、引用原文、回复全部、带附件、转发原附件
tools.forwardEmail: 转发指定邮件到指定收件人，支持自定义正文、主题、是否携带原附件
tools.deleteEmailById: 批量删除邮件（本地+远程IMAP），支持中文mailbox，失败时标记本地删除
tools.deleteTemplateById: 根据模版ID删除邮件模版
tools.markEmailAsRead: 批量将邮件状态更新为已读，并同步远程邮箱已读状态

tools.crawl_site_urls: 根据指定网站域名和深度，爬取该网站下的所有URL
tools.save_crawled_urls: 将指定网站域名下的URL保存到数据库
tools.query_crawled_urls: 查询数据库中指定网站域名下所有已爬取的URL
tools.generate_site_map: 为指定网站域名生成sitemap.xml网站地图

tools.getSoundDetailWithUrl: 根据关键词获取包含URL的白噪音详情，播放白噪声的时候调用这个工具获取URL

tools.list_examples: List SOLAPI SDK examples synced from official SDK repositories. Returns lightweight catalog entries (id, sdk, language, category, title, htmlUrl). Use the returned id with get_example to fetch full source code. Filter by sdk and/or category, or pass q for substring match against title/path/category.
tools.get_example: Fetch the full source code of a SOLAPI SDK example by id (as returned by list_examples). Returns the file contents along with metadata (sdk, language, category, htmlUrl). For Java/Kotlin Spring demos and Next.js/Laravel/Django integration entries, the id maps to a controller file or README; explore the htmlUrl directory for sibling files.

tools.salesforce_search_objects: Search for Salesforce standard and custom objects by name pattern. Examples: 'Account' will find Account, AccountHistory; 'Order' will find WorkOrder, ServiceOrder__c etc.
tools.salesforce_describe_object: Get detailed schema metadata including all fields, relationships, and field properties of any Salesforce object. Examples: 'Account' shows all Account fields including custom fields; 'Case' shows all Case fields including relationships to Account, Contact etc.
tools.salesforce_query_records:
Query records from any Salesforce object using SOQL, including relationship queries.

NOTE: For queries with GROUP BY, aggregate functions (COUNT, SUM, AVG, etc.), or HAVING clauses, use salesforce_aggregate_query instead.

Examples:
1. Parent-to-child query (e.g., Account with Contacts):
   - objectName: "Account"
   - fields: ["Name", "(SELECT Id, FirstName, LastName FROM Contacts)"]

2. Child-to-parent query (e.g., Contact with Account details):
   - objectName: "Contact"
   - fields: ["FirstName", "LastName", "Account.Name", "Account.Industry"]

3. Multiple level query (e.g., Contact -> Account -> Owner):
   - objectName: "Contact"
   - fields: ["Name", "Account.Name", "Account.Owner.Name"]

4. Related object filtering:
   - objectName: "Contact"
   - fields: ["Name", "Account.Name"]
   - whereClause: "Account.Industry = 'Technology'"

Note: When using relationship fields:
- Use dot notation for parent relationships (e.g., "Account.Name")
- Use subqueries in parentheses for child relationships (e.g., "(SELECT Id FROM Contacts)")
- Custom relationship fields end in "__r" (e.g., "CustomObject__r.Name")
tools.salesforce_aggregate_query:
Execute SOQL queries with GROUP BY, aggregate functions, and statistical analysis. Use this tool for queries that summarize and group data rather than returning individual records.

NOTE: For regular queries without GROUP BY or aggregates, use salesforce_query_records instead.

This tool handles:
1. GROUP BY queries (single/multiple fields, related objects, date functions)
2. Aggregate functions: COUNT(), COUNT_DISTINCT(), SUM(), AVG(), MIN(), MAX()
3. HAVING clauses for filtering grouped results
4. Date/time grouping: CALENDAR_YEAR(), CALENDAR_MONTH(), CALENDAR_QUARTER(), FISCAL_YEAR(), FISCAL_QUARTER()

Examples:
1. Count opportunities by stage:
   - objectName: "Opportunity"
   - selectFields: ["StageName", "COUNT(Id) OpportunityCount"]
   - groupByFields: ["StageName"]

2. Analyze cases by priority and status:
   - objectName: "Case"
   - selectFields: ["Priority", "Status", "COUNT(Id) CaseCount", "AVG(Days_Open__c) AvgDaysOpen"]
   - groupByFields: ["Priority", "Status"]

3. Count contacts by account industry:
   - objectName: "Contact"
   - selectFields: ["Account.Industry", "COUNT(Id) ContactCount"]
   - groupByFields: ["Account.Industry"]

4. Quarterly opportunity analysis:
   - objectName: "Opportunity"
   - selectFields: ["CALENDAR_YEAR(CloseDate) Year", "CALENDAR_QUARTER(CloseDate) Quarter", "SUM(Amount) Revenue"]
   - groupByFields: ["CALENDAR_YEAR(CloseDate)", "CALENDAR_QUARTER(CloseDate)"]

5. Find accounts with more than 10 opportunities:
   - objectName: "Opportunity"
   - selectFields: ["Account.Name", "COUNT(Id) OpportunityCount"]
   - groupByFields: ["Account.Name"]
   - havingClause: "COUNT(Id) > 10"

Important Rules:
- All non-aggregate fields in selectFields MUST be included in groupByFields
- Use whereClause to filter rows BEFORE grouping
- Use havingClause to filter AFTER grouping (for aggregate conditions)
- ORDER BY can only use fields from groupByFields or aggregate functions
- OFFSET is not supported with GROUP BY in Salesforce
tools.salesforce_dml_records:
Perform data manipulation operations on Salesforce records:
  - insert: Create new records
  - update: Modify existing records (requires Id)
  - delete: Remove records (requires Id)
  - upsert: Insert or update based on external ID field
  Examples: Insert new Accounts, Update Case status, Delete old records, Upsert based on custom external ID
tools.salesforce_manage_object:
Create new custom objects or modify existing ones in Salesforce:

  - Update: Modify existing object settings, labels, sharing model
  Examples: Create Customer_Feedback__c object, Update object sharing settings
  Note: Changes affect metadata and require proper permissions
tools.salesforce_manage_field:
Create new custom fields or modify existing fields on any Salesforce object:
  - Field Types: Text, Number, Date, Lookup, Master-Detail, Picklist etc.
  - Properties: Required, Unique, External ID, Length, Scale etc.
  - Relationships: Create lookups and master-detail relationships
  - Automatically grants Field Level Security to System Administrator (or specified profiles)
  Examples: Add Rating__c picklist to Account, Create Account lookup on Custom Object
  Note: Use grantAccessTo parameter to specify profiles, defaults to System Administrator
tools.salesforce_manage_field_permissions:
Manage Field Level Security (Field Permissions) for custom and standard fields.
  - Grant or revoke read/edit access to fields for specific profiles or permission sets

  - Bulk update permissions for multiple profiles
  
  Examples:
  1. Grant System Administrator access to a field
  2. Give read-only access to a field for specific profiles
  3. Check which profiles have access to a field
tools.salesforce_write_apex:
Create or update Apex classes in Salesforce.
  
Examples:
1. Create a new Apex class:
   {
     "operation": "create",
     "className": "AccountService",
     "apiVersion": "58.0",
     "body": "public class AccountService { public static void updateAccounts() { /* implementation */ } }"
   }

2. Update an existing Apex class:
   {
     "operation": "update",
     "className": "AccountService",
     "body": "public class AccountService { public static void updateAccounts() { /* updated implementation */ } }"
   }

Notes:
- The operation must be either 'create' or 'update'
- For 'create' operations, className and body are required
- For 'update' operations, className and body are required
- apiVersion is optional for 'create' (defaults to the latest version)
- The body must be valid Apex code
- The className in the body must match the className parameter
- Status information is returned after successful operations
tools.salesforce_write_apex_trigger:
Create or update Apex triggers in Salesforce.
  
Examples:
1. Create a new Apex trigger:
   {
     "operation": "create",
     "triggerName": "AccountTrigger",
     "objectName": "Account",
     "apiVersion": "58.0",
     "body": "trigger AccountTrigger on Account (before insert, before update) { /* implementation */ }"
   }

2. Update an existing Apex trigger:
   {
     "operation": "update",
     "triggerName": "AccountTrigger",
     "body": "trigger AccountTrigger on Account (before insert, before update, after update) { /* updated implementation */ }"
   }

Notes:
- The operation must be either 'create' or 'update'
- For 'create' operations, triggerName, objectName, and body are required
- For 'update' operations, triggerName and body are required
- apiVersion is optional for 'create' (defaults to the latest version)
- The body must be valid Apex trigger code
- The triggerName in the body must match the triggerName parameter
- The objectName in the body must match the objectName parameter (for 'create')
- Status information is returned after successful operations
tools.salesforce_execute_anonymous:
Execute anonymous Apex code in Salesforce.
  
Examples:
1. Execute simple Apex code:
   {
     "apexCode": "System.debug('Hello World');"
   }

2. Execute Apex code with variables:
   {
     "apexCode": "List<Account> accounts = [SELECT Id, Name FROM Account LIMIT 5]; for(Account a : accounts) { System.debug(a.Name); }"
   }

3. Execute Apex with debug logs:
   {
     "apexCode": "System.debug(LoggingLevel.INFO, 'Processing accounts...'); List<Account> accounts = [SELECT Id FROM Account LIMIT 10]; System.debug(LoggingLevel.INFO, 'Found ' + accounts.size() + ' accounts');",
     "logLevel": "DEBUG"
   }

Notes:
- The apexCode parameter is required and must contain valid Apex code
- The code is executed in an anonymous context and does not persist
- The logLevel parameter is optional (defaults to 'DEBUG')
- Execution results include compilation success/failure, execution success/failure, and debug logs
- For security reasons, some operations may be restricted based on user permissions
- This tool can be used for data operations or updates when there are no other specific tools available
- When users request data queries or updates that aren't directly supported by other tools, this tool can be used if the operation is achievable using Apex code
tools.salesforce_manage_debug_logs:
Manage debug logs for Salesforce users - enable, disable, or retrieve logs.
  
Examples:
1. Enable debug logs for a user:
   {
     "operation": "enable",
     "username": "user@example.com",
     "logLevel": "DEBUG",
     "expirationTime": 30
   }

2. Disable debug logs for a user:
   {
     "operation": "disable",
     "username": "user@example.com"
   }

3. Retrieve debug logs for a user:
   {
     "operation": "retrieve",
     "username": "user@example.com",
     "limit": 5
   }

4. Retrieve a specific log with full content:
   {
     "operation": "retrieve",
     "username": "user@example.com",
     "logId": "07L1g000000XXXXEAA0",
     "includeBody": true
   }

Notes:
- The operation must be one of: 'enable', 'disable', or 'retrieve'
- The username parameter is required for all operations
- For 'enable' operation, logLevel is optional (defaults to 'DEBUG')
- Log levels: NONE, ERROR, WARN, INFO, DEBUG, FINE, FINER, FINEST
- expirationTime is optional for 'enable' operation (minutes until expiration, defaults to 30)
- limit is optional for 'retrieve' operation (maximum number of logs to return, defaults to 10)
- logId is optional for 'retrieve' operation (to get a specific log)
- includeBody is optional for 'retrieve' operation (to include the full log content, defaults to false)
- The tool validates that the specified user exists before performing operations
- If logLevel is not specified when enabling logs, the tool will ask for clarification

tools.get_all_docs:
Provide all Next.js documentation URLs for AI agents.

Auto-trigger guidance (for clients):
- Run when the user asks about 'Next.js', 'Nextjs', 'Next', or mentions topics like 'App Router', 'Pages Router', 'Route Handlers', 'data fetching', 'deployment', 'turbopack', 'Vercel'.
- Run when the user reports errors containing keywords like 'Next.js error', 'build error', 'routing error', 'hydration error', 'module not found', 'next.config.js', 'middleware', 'Image', 'Link', 'Route Handler'.
- Run when an active file path suggests a Next.js app, e.g. 'next.config.js', 'app/**', 'pages/**', 'middleware.ts/js', or imports starting with 'next/'.

Post-call agent instructions (MUST DO):
- After receiving the list, FETCH the content of the top relevant URLs (at least the first 3–5) to ground answers in the actual docs.
- Use standard HTTP GET with a 10s timeout, follow redirects, and limit concurrency to 3 to be polite.
- Prefer pages whose title/URL matches the user's query or error message; summarize only after fetching.
- If fetching fails, try the next candidate URL and report which ones were fetched.
This tool returns a comprehensive list so the agent can pick and fetch the most relevant docs.

tools.ask-question: Asks a question about an application and gets an answer with supporting context. This tool uses the agent service to provide comprehensive answers with relevant documentation. Provide both an application slug and a specific question.
tools.search-documentation: Searches documentation for an application to get relevant context. Documentation includes information about application resources, concepts, stories and known solutions. Provide both an application slug and a specific query.
tools.add-ticket-comment: Adds a comment to an existing ticket. This tool allows adding a comment to a specific ticket with proper attribution.
tools.add-documentation: Creates a new knowledge ticket with documentation content. Only use this tool if a comment cannot be added directly to a ticket. This tool creates a knowledge ticket that can be used to store and organize documentation, procedures, guides, or any other knowledge-based content for future reference.
tools.get-ticket-details: Gets the details of a ticket. The ticket reference must be provided. This tool will provide the initial description of the ticket and any comments that users have made on the ticket.
tools.start-ticket: Starts working on a ticket by retrieving ticket details, and providing next-step guidance. This tool sets up a 30-minute session window during which other MCP tools will automatically provide contextual next steps.
tools.get-git-branch-for-ticket: Gets the git branch to be used for development work on this ticket. All commits for this ticket must use this branch. Git branches must stay ahead of main.
tools.mark-ticket-as-blocked: Marks a ticket as blocked with a specified reason. This tool will load the ticket, add a comment with the blocking reason, and set the ticket status to blocked.
tools.update-action-item: Updates the status of an action item in a ticket. This tool finds a specific action item in the ticket or its comments and updates its status to INCOMPLETE, INPROGRESS, or COMPLETED. Action items are matched case-insensitively on a leading prefix of their text (provide enough characters to be unique, for example the first 20), and when setting INPROGRESS or COMPLETED already-completed items are skipped so the next outstanding match is updated.
tools.get-resource-list: Gets a list of resources for an application. Resources include system dependencies, infrastructure, documentation and policies.
tools.get-resource-details: Gets detailed information about a specific resource by name and group. Resource names can be identified by using get-resource-list. Special resources include: Application Map, Style Guide, Tech Patterns, Database Schema, User Guide
tools.answer-question: Answers a question that was previously asked with a TECHNICAL or BUSINESS question type. Questions are identified by their six-character reference code.
tools.raise-ticket: Creates a new ticket and returns information that may be useful when implementing the ticket.  Tickets represent a unit-of-work that is being done for an application. After the ticket has been raised, comments can be added to the ticket using the add-ticket-comment tool.
tools.get-skill: Retrieves a skill workflow by code or name. Skills are reusable capabilities that AI agents can execute during workflow execution. Parameter accepts either the short skill code or full skill name.
tools.find-available-skills: Searches for the most relevant skills using a semantic search query and returns their codes, names, and descriptions. Use this to discover which skills are available before loading a specific skill with get-skill.
tools.attach-screenshot: Attaches a screenshot or image file from the local filesystem to a ticket. The tool reads the file from the provided path, encodes it, and uploads it as an attachment to the specified ticket. Supports common image formats (PNG, JPG, GIF, WebP).

tools.testsprite_bootstrap: BEFORE calling this tool, check if .testsprite/config.json exists. If config.json EXISTS, DO NOT call this tool - proceed directly with other tools instead. This tool is ONLY for first-time project initialization when no configuration exists. NEVER call for: adding new test cases, modifying tests, re-running tests, or any operation on an already-configured project. Note: this MCP tests a locally-running app (it tunnels your local server). If the change is only available at a deployed URL (preview/staging/prod), use the TestSprite CLI instead — it's the tool that can reach a deployed target.
tools.testsprite_generate_code_summary: Analyze the project repository and summarize the codebase.
tools.testsprite_generate_frontend_test_plan: Generate test plan for frontend test.
tools.testsprite_generate_backend_test_plan: Generate a backend test plan with Testsprite.
tools.testsprite_generate_code_and_execute: Generate and execute tests. Before calling this tool, ensure the local project is running — preferably in production mode (e.g. `npm run build && npm run start` for Next.js, `npm run build && npm run preview` for Vite). If you started the project with a production build+serve command, set serverMode to 'production' (note: serverMode is also auto-detected from the running process). If running a dev server (e.g. npm run dev), leave serverMode as default — frontend tests will be limited to 15 high-priority tests to prevent dev server overload. If local server is running and test plan is already generated, call this tool directly — DO NOT call testsprite_bootstrap first. AI assistant analyzes the test results and saves a markdown report. This runs against your locally-running server. To verify a change only reachable at a deployed URL, use the TestSprite CLI instead.
tools.testsprite_open_test_result_dashboard: Open an interactive web dashboard to review and modify finished test cases. Use this tool when users want to review test results, fix failing tests, or modify test steps. The dashboard displays all test cases with their execution status, allows users to view test details, edit individual steps, and re-run tests from any step. Prerequisites: (1) Tests must have been generated first using 'testsprite_generate_code_and_execute', (2) Local project must be running on the configured port for re-running tests.

tools.create-instance-secrets:
An Instance Secret is a DataOS Resource(https://dataos.info/resources/) designed for securely storing sensitive information at the DataOS Instance-level. 
The primary purpose of an Instance Secret is to address the inherent exposure risk associated with directly embedding such confidential data within application code or manifest files (YAML configuration files). 
This includes usernames, passwords, certificates, tokens, and keys. Instance Secrets establish a critical segregation between sensitive data and Resource definitions. This division minimizes inadvertent exposure during various Resource management phases, including creation, viewing, or editing.

Complete configuration details: https://dataos.info/resources/instance_secret/configurations/
tools.create-depot-source:
Depot in DataOS is a Resource used to connect different data sources to DataOS by abstracting the complexities associated with the underlying source system (including protocols, credentials, and connection schemas). 
It enables users to establish connections and retrieve data from various data sources, such as file systems (e.g., AWS S3, Google GCS, Azure Blob Storage), data lake systems, database systems (e.g., Redshift, SnowflakeDB, Bigquery, Postgres), and event systems (e.g., Kafka, Pulsar) without moving the data.
tools.create-flare-workflow:
Flare Workflow in DataOS is a declarative stack for large-scale data processing using Apache Spark. It provides comprehensive solutions for data ingestion, transformation, enrichment, profiling, quality assessment, and syndication on both batch and incremental data.

Flare Workflows support multiple job types:
- **Batch Jobs**: Process all data in each run, ensuring consistent performance. Ideal for small to medium datasets
- **Incremental Jobs**: Process only changed data since last run, reducing computation and latency for large datasets
- **Data Quality Jobs**: Validate data using business-specific assertions to ensure fitness-for-purpose
- **Data Profiling Jobs**: Assess data structure, completeness, and validity with automatic fingerprinting

Key Features:
- Declarative YAML-based programming paradigm
- Support for 16+ data sources (S3, BigQuery, Snowflake, Kafka, etc.)
- Advanced transformations with SQL and built-in functions
- Comprehensive data quality and profiling capabilities
- Iceberg table optimization and maintenance
- Auto-scaling and resource management

Examples:
- ETL pipelines from data lakes to warehouses
- Real-time data ingestion and transformation
- Data quality validation and monitoring
- Cross-platform data syndication
- Advanced analytics and feature engineering
tools.create-quality-workflow:
Soda Workflow in DataOS is a declarative tool for scheduled data quality testing within and beyond data pipelines, extending its capabilities, enhancing data observability and reliability across one or more datasets. It enables you to use the Soda Checks Language (SodaCL) to turn user-defined inputs into aggregated SQL queries.

Soda supports comprehensive data quality checks across multiple categories:
- **Accuracy**: Row counts, value ranges, calculations, cross-dataset validation
- **Completeness**: Missing value detection, required field validation
- **Consistency**: Cross-table reference checks, data format consistency  
- **Freshness**: Data recency and staleness detection
- **Schema**: Column presence, data types, structural validation
- **Uniqueness**: Duplicate detection and primary key validation
- **Validity**: Format validation, range checks, custom business rules

Examples:
- Basic checks: row_count between 100 and 1000, missing_count(email) = 0
- Advanced checks: values in (city) must exist in cities (name), freshness(updated_at) < 1d
- Schema validation: required columns, data types, forbidden columns
tools.create-scanner-workflow:
Scanner Workflow in DataOS is a Stack that functions as a metadata extractor for scheduled or one-time metadata extraction jobs. It enables users to pull information from various data sources and subsequently store this extracted metadata in the Metis DB. These sources include data systems, BI tools, dashboard and visualization tools, databases, data lake systems, messaging services, pipelines, ML-model stores, and many more.

Scanner Workflows support comprehensive metadata extraction:
- **Database Sources**: PostgreSQL, MySQL, Snowflake, BigQuery, Redshift, Oracle, SQL Server
- **Messaging Systems**: Kafka, Pulsar, EventHub
- **Search Engines**: Elasticsearch, OpenSearch
- **NoSQL Databases**: MongoDB
- **Data Lakes**: Iceberg, Delta Lake, Hudi
- **BI Tools**: Tableau, PowerBI, Looker
- **DataOS Resources**: Workflows, Depots, Services, Policies

Examples:
- Database scanner: Extract table schemas, relationships from PostgreSQL/MySQL/Snowflake
- Kafka scanner: Extract topic metadata and schemas  
- Data Quality scanner: Extract quality check results and lineage
- DataOS Resources scanner: Extract metadata from DataOS resources like workflows, depots
tools.create-bundle:
Bundle in DataOS is a Resource that serves as a declarative and standardized mechanism for deploying a collection of Resources, Data Products, or applications in a single operation. 
It empowers data developers with the capability to programmatically orchestrate the deployment, scheduling, creation, and dismantling of code and infrastructure resources linked to these Data Products and applications in a unified manner.

A Bundle aggregates various DataOS Resources into a flattened directed acyclic graph (DAG), where each node represents a distinct DataOS Resource, interconnected through dependency relationships.
Examples: Deploy a complete data pipeline with depot connections, data ingestion workflows, quality checks, and scanners all orchestrated together.
tools.create-data-product:
Data Product in DataOS is a curated, reusable, and governed dataset that provides business value and is designed to be consumed by various applications, analytics, and decision-making processes. 
Data Products encapsulate data, metadata, transformation logic, quality checks, and consumption interfaces, making data assets more discoverable, accessible, and trustworthy.

Data Products can be versioned (v1alpha, v1beta) and support various inputs, outputs, resources, and consumption ports like Lens (semantic layer) and Talos (APIs).
tools.create-lens-manifest:
Lens Manifest is used to deploy Lens resources on DataOS, providing a semantic modeling layer over your data sources. Lens enables business users to access and analyze data through a unified interface while maintaining governance and performance.

Lens provides:
- **Semantic Modeling**: Create logical views of your data with dimensions, measures, and metrics
- **Multi-Source Support**: Connect to various data sources (Minerva, Themis, Depot, Flash)
- **Auto-scaling**: Automatically scale API instances based on workload
- **High Availability**: Distribute workloads across nodes, zones, or regions
- **Performance Optimization**: Built-in caching and query optimization
- **Security**: Role-based access control and data governance

Key Components:
- **API Instance**: Processes incoming requests and connects to databases
- **Worker**: Manages background refresh and cache invalidation
- **Router**: Handles query planning and distribution between API and workers

Deployment Features:
- Support for public and private code repositories
- Flexible resource allocation (CPU/Memory)
- Environment variable configuration
- Auto-scaling based on CPU/Memory utilization
- High availability across multiple zones/regions
tools.create-lens-sql:
Lens SQL Tool for preparing view models in DataOS Lens semantic layer using SQL selections and filters.
This tool helps create SQL queries for Lens model views that reference dimensions, measures, and segments from multiple logical tables.

Lens operates as a logical modeling layer for accessing tabular data in data warehouses/lakehouses, extending physical tables into logical tables with measures and relationships.
Examples: Create entity-first views (customer profiles, product analytics) or metrics-first views (conversion rates, revenue tracking) with proper SQL selections and joins.
tools.create-lens-segments:
Lens Segments are reusable filters defined in the segment section within table manifests of the semantic model. They allow stakeholders to apply common filtering logic consistently across multiple queries, similar to how a WHERE clause works in SQL.

Segments are essential for:
- **Reusable Filtering**: Apply the same filter conditions across multiple queries and dashboards
- **Data Governance**: Enforce row-level security and data access policies
- **Performance**: Pre-defined filters that can be optimized by the query engine
- **Consistency**: Ensure consistent business logic across different analyses

Key Features:
- SQL-based filter expressions using {TABLE} placeholder
- Support for complex logical operations (AND, OR, LIKE, IN)
- User group-based security policies
- Row-level data access control
- Integration with Lens views and queries

Use segments when you notice the same filter conditions being applied repeatedly across multiple queries or dashboards.
tools.create-lens-table:
Lens Table Tool for creating comprehensive table definitions in DataOS Lens semantic layer.
This tool helps create logical table definitions with dimensions, measures, segments, and joins that form the foundation of Lens data models.

Lens tables are logical constructs that define core business entities (Customer, Product, Sales) by extending physical tables with dimensions (descriptive attributes), measures (aggregated values), segments (filters), and relationships (joins).
Examples: Create customer tables with demographics and lifetime value, product tables with categories and inventory metrics, sales tables with revenue calculations and time-based segments.
tools.create-lens-views:
Lens Views serve as a layer atop the data graph of tables, presenting an abstraction of the entire data model with which consumers can interact. Views are essential for defining metrics and providing a simplified interface for end-users to interact with key business metrics.

There are two main approaches for designing views:

1. **Entity-first approach**: Views built around entities (customer, product, transaction) as denormalized tables bringing measures and dimensions from different tables to fully describe the entity.

2. **Metrics-first approach**: Views focused on specific performance metrics, each containing one key measure with relevant dimensions for grouping and filtering. Each view represents a specific business metric over time.

Views reference dimensions, measures, and segments from multiple logical tables but don't have any measures, dimensions, or segments of their own.
tools.create-lens-user-groups:
Lens User Groups are used to manage both data access and API scopes, which control access to specific functionalities and endpoints in the Lens semantic layer. This forms part of the access policy, ensuring users interact only with the data and features they are authorized to use.

User Groups provide:
- **API Scope Management**: Control access to specific REST API endpoints (meta, data, graphql)
- **Data Access Control**: Define who can access what data and functionality
- **Granular Permissions**: Support for least privilege principle
- **Group Priority**: First-listed group takes precedence when users belong to multiple groups
- **Integration with Data Policies**: Work with dimension masking and segment filtering

Key Features:
- Flexible user inclusion/exclusion patterns
- Support for wildcard (*) and specific user IDs
- API scope-based endpoint access control
- Integration with Lens Studio Interface
- Support for organizational and regulatory compliance

User groups extend governance to the Lens Studio Interface, where access to specific tabs and functionalities can be controlled, supporting compliance with organizational and regulatory standards.
